questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Bologna is a great city for studying. It is a young city and like Aarhus in size. Moreover, the train connections to cities like Milan, Florence, Naples, Rome and many more are good, which means, that there are many cultural opportunities nearby.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The websites concerning exchange information and courses are not always intuitive, but once you get to know them, you will know, where to find the information, you need. University of Bologna also have an e-mail for incoming students, but the answer time might vary.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a couple of e-mails on, how to check-in and get a study-ID.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not difficult to find housing off campus, but prices are similar to the ones in Copenhagen. Moreover, a tip is to be in good time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It creates a good relation to the city and life outside of university.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The semester begins in the middle of September, and the courses are published in the beginning of July. I would recommend to be a bit flexible, since some of the courses are of limited capacity and may be full. The university sends an e-mail to your UniBo-mail with a website, where you fill in your course wishes. This all has to add up with your pre-approvals from University of Copenhagen. It can be a confusing process, but University of Bologna are not very strict with the deadline of your course choice, since you have to register for the exam and not the course in the end.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: University of Bologna has an e-mail and a physical office, which can help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesfull overall. However, I am a bachelor student, and it is important to notice, that University of Bologna do not allow bachelor students to attend master courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would suggest to take a look at the courses from last year, since it offers more time for both deciding and getting pre-approvals. The courses did not change that much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: University of Bologna does not allow bachelor students to attend master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Both University of Copenhagen and University of Bologna have classical lectures. However, University of Copenhagen also offers weekly exercise classes, which University of Bologna only does one or two times per semester and close to the exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Political Sociology (8 ECTS)
Industrial Organization (9 ECTS)
Monetary Economics: Theory of Money and Liquidity (4 ECTS)
Principles of Management (9 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Industrial Organization was very interesting to me regarding competition, and I would really recommend it. Also Applied Political Sociology was a good course with critical perspectives on data and its origin.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation was a bit more expensive than expected, when visiting other Italian cities.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in both supermarkets and restaurants is a lot cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university has a department similar to KU Studenteridræt with many different activities. They also host different kinds of events. The Erasmus Network in Bologna also hosts different events and trips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I went to the Italian language course, which was a great opportunity to both meet other international student and learn more about both culture and language.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed going on trips to other Italian cities. By train, most of the larger cities are reachable in around 3 or 4 hours. Also, hiking is a great activity for the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Of course it is a different language and environment, but the basics of the culture are not relatively far from the Danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There are many cozy cafes and libraries, where many both local and international students go, so I would go there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The university hours are a bit different, which means, that classes usually do not start at 8 in the morning, and that it is not abnormal with classes ending at 7 or 9 in the evening.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the calmness and non-stressfullness of the culture and the amazing food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be in good time with planning, but not too good.
You will not regret going on exchange, since it is great.
Prioritize eating out.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Around 1 or 2 days per month, classes were cancelled because of bad weather (often rain). They find online solutions or similar, but be prepared for changes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is a big privilege to be able to experience another city than your hometown from the inside or as close to the inside as possible. It creates a lot of perspective on both the world and your own country. Also a great privilege to feel at home in another city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some of the paperworks did create challenges at some points.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
